verbatim_locators.note: COVERAGE: whole article read, Tables 1 and 2 read cell by cell, Figure 1 inspected as an image. Case reports have no methods or limitations sections as such: the Discussion carries both and is read; the reference list (24) was screened for integrity, with ref 18 identified as the source of the reference ranges and not read.

entries.proposition: DESIGN: two adult women with SCN1A-related Dravet syndrome and parkinsonism; DAT SPECT and CSF monoamine metabolites measured once; levodopa-carbidopa started in both; no control group of Dravet patients without parkinsonism (the authors name this as the key limitation).
entries.snippet: The lack of CSF data in patients with DS who do not have parkinsonism is an important limitation of our study.

entries.proposition: Table 2 reports four CSF analytes per case against the quoted reference range: HVA 36.6 and 79.3 against 145 to 324; 5-HIAA 20.4 and 52.2 against 67 to 140 nmol/L.

THE NORADRENALINE ARM IS IN THE TABLE AND NOT IN THE TEXT: CSF MHPG, the main central noradrenaline metabolite, is 27.7 in Case 1 (below the quoted 35 to 65) and 40.7 in Case 2 (inside it); the abstract, discussion and conclusion speak only of HVA and 5-HIAA.

Discussion wording: HVA and 5-HIAA levels significantly lower than the published reference values; the evidence is one value per patient against a published range, with no test and n of 2 (the abstract says the same).
entries.snippet: In both cases, HVA and 5‐HIAA levels were significantly lower than the reference values in the published report

entries.proposition: The authors assert the CSF results were reliable because no seizures or other confounders preceded sampling, although Case 2 had frequent seizures into adulthood and the interval from the last seizure and the medication state (valproate, fenfluramine; aripiprazole in Case 1) at sampling are not given.
entries.snippet: No epileptic seizures and other causes that can affect the CSF results occurred before the examination; therefore, the measurement results were considered reliable.

entries.proposition: Medication in Table 1 includes fenfluramine (a serotonin-releasing drug) in Case 2 and aripiprazole in Case 1; risperidone and valproate were stopped in Case 1 at admission; whether these altered the CSF metabolites is not addressed.
entries.snippet: First, we considered the possibility of drug‐induced parkinsonism and discontinued valproic acid (VPA) and risperidone; however, bradykinesia, rigidity, and tremor persisted

entries.proposition: DAT SPECT was normal in both patients (specific binding ratios 10.49 and 9.58 in Case 1; 9.32 and 9.88 in Case 2), which the authors read as intact presynaptic dopaminergic terminals.
entries.snippet: No decrease in the striatal signals was observed (Figure 1C).

entries.proposition: Figure 1 C and D show symmetric intense striatal uptake on the colour scale in both patients, consistent with the stated ratios; panels A and B are T1 MRI with non-specific atrophy per the caption.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1: panels A and B axial T1 MRI of Case 1 and Case 2; panels C and D DAT SPECT of Case 1 and Case 2, two bilateral bright striatal comma-shaped uptakes on a 0 to 5 BP colour scale, symmetric.

experimental_context.system: two adult women with SCN1A Dravet syndrome and parkinsonism
experimental_context.genotype: SCN1A heterozygous missense, one classified uncertain significance and one likely pathogenic
experimental_context.endpoint: MRI and DAT SPECT striatal binding ratio

entries.proposition: Levodopa response: Case 1 improved on levodopa-carbidopa with the benefit continuing about a year; Case 2 had only started a low dose. The authors recognise previous reports of response as inconclusive and age-dependent.
entries.snippet: previously, the efficacy of levodopa's effect on parkinsonism in patients with DS has been reported as inconclusive.

entries.proposition: Internal inconsistencies of age: Case 1 is called 29 years in the text and 28 in Table 1; the abstract places onset of parkinsonism around 30 for both, while the text dates Case 1 onset at 27 and Case 2 slowness and hypomimia in the early 20s.
entries.snippet: Case 1 was a 29‐year‐old woman who manifested a typical clinical course of DS and was later diagnosed genetically.
